title: Payoff: latency + unit-econ hypothesis bank
content:
Purpose:
Quick internal bank of hypothesis-style claims and concrete proof angles tying latency and per-token economics to customer ROI. This is intentionally compact — the goal is to provide short, testable snippets for sales/field experiments, one-pagers, and A/B pitch variants.

Status/context: draft. Pulls from recent lab runs (perf bench PR 93), Dedicated capacity cost model, and early Private deployments where batch/cache settings were tuned. Assumptions noted inline; each claim needs a source artifact (bench run id or billing calc) before final copy.

Executive claim hypotheses (short, testable):
- "Reduce 95th latency and average token cost in tandem — customers get faster responses and 20–40% lower per-100k-token spend compared to naive endpoint configs."
- "For chat-first SaaS, request-level KV/prefix caching + modest batching yields 30–60% per-session cost savings with <5% p50 latency delta."
- "Smart routing (fallback to quantized model variants) maintains availability while reducing tail cost by ~25% under load peaks."

Proof-point buckets (how we'll prove each claim):
1) Microbenchmarks: p50/p95/p99 generation latency for 3 model classes (small/med/large) across our runtime vs baseline containerized endpoints. Include token/s.
2) Economics simulation: real workload replay (customer traces) to compute per-session and per-1M-token cost for three configs: a) naive 1-request-per-call b) batching+caching c) batching+caching+quantization.
3) End-to-end customer scenario: instrumented pilot (1–2 customers) to show balanced metric set: latency SLO attainment, per-session $ savings, and quality delta (automatic eval on held prompt set).

Concrete sample hypothesis (example math):
Scenario: mid-market helpdesk chat app. 2,000 active concurrent sessions during peak. Average prompt+response = 200 tokens (50 user, 150 model). Daily peak sustained for 3 hours.
Assumptions (conservative):
- Baseline competitor endpoint cost per 1k tokens = $0.60 (hypothetical)
- Our naive hosted endpoint (no batching/cache) runtime cost = $0.45 per 1k tokens
- With batching + KV cache + quantization policy applied: effective token cost = $0.27 per 1k tokens (40% reduction from our naive runtime, 55% vs competitor)
Compute (1 day peak): 2,000 sessions * 200 tokens = 400k tokens per request-wave. For 3 hours sustained at 1 request per minute per session -> 180 waves -> 400k * 180 = 72M tokens.
Cost comparison (one peak day):
- Competitor: 72M / 1k * $0.60 = $43,200
- Redwood naive: 72M / 1k * $0.45 = $32,400
- Redwood optimized: 72M / 1k * $0.27 = $19,440
Delta: optimized vs competitor = $23,760 saved (55%).
Notes: these are illustrative. We need a recorded workload replay and cost model calibration (region, GPU amort, ops) to lock the final numbers.

Technical levers that enable the claims (short bullets for field):
- Aggressive but safe batching with latency SLO shaping (how many ms headroom we allow before dispatch).
- Prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts (session-level cache for multi-turn chat).
- Quantized model variants used as fallback for low-cost inference on non-sensitive calls or as primary for lower-quality-tolerance routes.
- Smart routing rules to route by customer tier / latency target / cost-budget.
- Autoscaling with burst smoothing to avoid expensive cold starts.

Quality/accuracy caveats and how we measure them:
- For each cost-lowering lever (batching, quantize), measure automated quality regression on canonical eval sets (ROUGE/BLEU not enough — use domain-specific heuristics + small human review sample).
- Define acceptable delta bands (e.g., <= 3% decrease in correctness for retrieval-augmented Q&A; <= 1% hallucination increase for structured output).

Competitive framing (simple archetypes and counter-angles):
- "Raw cloud vendor" (A): sells raw GPUs and endpoints; cheaper on list GPU price but lacks ops-level batching/caching and unified rollouts. Angle: Redwood’s runtime extracts unit-econ benefits that vendors don’t advertise — show end-to-end per-transaction $ not just GPU-hour.
- "API-first incumbents" (B): simple pricing-per-token but opaque latency/cost tradeoffs and limited deployment modes. Angle: highlight predictable Dedicated pricing + telemetry to prove p95 SLOs and per-route unit economics.
- "Self-hosted inference stacks" (C): high control, but ops burden and inconsistent perf. Angle: Redwood offers the same control (Private/Dedicated) with hardened runtime, fewer ops days and better observed p95.

Quick message snippets for sales experiments (A/Bable):
- A: "Get consistent sub-200ms p50 and 35% lower per-session cost — proven on chat workloads like yours."
- B: "We reduce the tokens you pay for through caching and smart batching — same quality, lower bill."
- C: "Reserve capacity with predictable unit economics and routing rules so peak events don’t spike costs."
Each variant should map to a one-pager with the math example above tailored to customer vertical.

Data gaps and immediate experiments (priority):
1) Run workload replays for three prospect verticals: chat/SaaS helpdesk, vector search + reranking, agent orchestration (tool calling). Owner: Marco. Target: replay + cost sheet by 2025-02-14.
2) Lab: p50/p95 bench across small/med/large with and without KV cache and 3 batching policies. Owner: Priya. Target: 2025-02-07.
3) Pilot: instrument one mid-market customer on Dedicated with cache+batches enabled and weekly telemetry digest. Owner: Dana. Target: scope w/ AE by 2025-02-10.

Risks / Qs (open):
- Are our cache hit-rate assumptions realistic for multi-tenant SaaS? Need real traces.
- Quantization quality varies by model family — need family-by-family thresholds.
- Sales may overpromise % savings — add guardrails in copy ("up to X%" with a footnote).

Appendix: quick checklist for a sales play one-pager
- 1 sentence claim + 1 line proof (bench run id or pilot)
- 2–3 bullets: how (batch/cache/quantize) and what it changes for the customer
- 1 concrete worked example (numbers adjusted per vertical)
- 1 footnote with measured quality delta or link to eval page
- Call to action: pilot with Dedicated or 2-week free replay analysis

TODOs:
- [ ] Attach replay IDs and perf-run artifacts to each claim (Marco)
- [ ] Draft 1-pager template (Asha)
- [ ] Run competitor cost-parity skim for common API incumbents (Dana)

Slack refs: #g2m-perf, #bench-results (see thread from 2025-01-10).

Bottom line: we can credibly claim "faster + cheaper" when we pair runtime levers (batching, caching, quantize) with transparent billing and per-route telemetry. This doc is a hypothesis bank — convert each line into a measurable experiment before shipping external collateral.
